item.title: Canada Council for the Arts: Arts Across Canada and Abroad, Public Outreach (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Canada Council for the Arts

Location: Activities must build audiences and public appreciation of the arts in Canada. Organisations must be incorporated or registered in Canada.

Award: CAD. Minimum and maximum are NOT published publicly; disclosed only in the client portal at arts-services.ca, which requires a login. No application fee. Council funds cannot cover expenses already covered by another revenue source; combined public grants must demonstrate complementarity.

Duration: Project-based; results usually notified within 5 months of the deadline.

Deadline: 14 Oct 2026

Funds activities that build connections between artists and diverse audiences and contribute to public appreciation and enjoyment of the arts in Canada. This is the closest Canada Council fit for running a public programme, a single festival edition, a talks series or audience-facing exhibition programming, as distinct from creating the artwork itself. It is open to arts festivals, presenters and event organisers under the Presenting organization profile, alongside Artistic organizations, Artistic groups and Arts supporting groups, and the profile explicitly includes visual arts festivals, biennials, triennials and quinquennials. Digital arts and new media, media arts, inter-arts, and music and sound art are named among funded practices, so experimental sound art and creative technology programming qualify. IMPORTANT: unlike the Circulation and Touring component, international organisations are NOT eligible for Public Outreach. The Council will not fund projects whose primary focus is educational, therapeutic, recreational or social service delivery, nor fundraising activities or prize and award ceremonies. Deadlines fall twice a year. The related Composite Activities component offers up to 3 years of support for bundled multi-project programmes and may suit a recurring festival arc better.

item.title: Canada Council for the Arts: Arts Across Canada and Abroad, Circulation and Touring (October 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Canada Council for the Arts

Location: Touring and circulation within Canada and internationally.

Award: CAD. Minimum and maximum are NOT published publicly; amounts are disclosed only inside the Council's client portal at arts-services.ca, which requires a login. No application fee. Council funds cannot cover expenses already covered by another revenue source, and combined municipal, provincial and federal grants must demonstrate complementarity of public support.

Duration: Project-based; results usually notified within 5 months of the deadline.

Deadline: 07 Oct 2026

Funds the circulation and touring of artists, exhibitions and artistic works by artists, groups and organisations from Canada, nationally and internationally. Media arts, digital arts and new media, inter-arts, and music and sound art are all explicitly named as supported practices, so experimental sound and creative technology work is in scope. This component sits inside Arts Across Canada and Abroad, the merged programme introduced in 2025 that replaced the separate Arts Across Canada and Arts Abroad programmes; the old Digital Now programme is discontinued. IMPORTANT AND UNDERUSED: non-Canadian organisations are eligible via the Foreign arts festival, biennale or book fair profile, defined as an incorporated organisation headquartered outside Canada running an international media arts festival, an international literary or storytelling festival, an international book fair, or a major international visual arts biennial, triennial or quinquennial. That support is restricted to presenting Canadian media, literary or visual artists and their work, and it is not advertised on the programme page. For digital and media arts, requests must be for work independent of the commercial film, television and video game industries, and only the creator or director may apply, not producers or production companies. Deadlines run three times a year. The sister component Representation and Promotion has continuous rolling intake and the same foreign-festival eligibility.

Open call details

item.title: Structurist Creative Research Fellowship (4th round)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Saskatchewan Art Galleries and Collection

Location: Saskatoon, Canada (travel and accommodation covered for the Saskatoon component). Open internationally, any career stage.

Award: Project budget up to CAD 20,000, plus travel and accommodation for the Saskatoon research component. No application fee.

Duration: Research-creation fellowship around The Structurist journal archive.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The University of Saskatchewan Art Galleries offer the Structurist Creative Research Fellowship, supporting art-and-science research-creation engaging The Structurist, the art and architecture journal published at the university from 1960 to 2010. The fellowship provides a project budget of up to CAD 20,000 plus travel and accommodation for the Saskatoon component. Open internationally at any career stage. Deadline 31 August 2026.

item.title: Al Purdy A-frame Association: Al and Eurithe Purdy Residency 2027
item.description:
Organisation: The Al Purdy A-frame Association

Location: Ameliasburgh, Prince Edward County, Ontario, Canada. Canadian citizens or permanent residents only.

Award: CAD 750 per week stipend plus paid return travel to Ameliasburgh (funding subject to the Association's fundraising and Canada Council matching). Terms of 3 to 12 weeks. No application fee.

Duration: 3 to 12 weeks

Deadline: 18 Sep 2026

The Al Purdy A-frame Residency offers Canadian writers time and space to work at the historic A-frame home built by poet Al Purdy and his wife Eurithe on Roblin Lake in Ameliasburgh, Prince Edward County, Ontario. Poetry is prioritized, but all writers are welcome. SUPPORT: CAD 750 per week stipend and paid return travel (subject to the Association's fundraising and Canada Council matching); residencies run 3 to 12 weeks. ELIGIBILITY: Canadian citizens or permanent residents only. DEADLINE: 18 September 2026 (postmark, or 4:00pm PT for electronic submissions). Apply via the residency page.

Open call details

item.title: SAT x LAB7: Performing Arts and Technology Research-Creation Residency 2026 (Montreal)
item.description:
Organisation: Societe des arts technologiques (SAT) in partnership with LAB7 / 7 Fingers (Les 7 Doigts)

Location: Montreal, Canada. Open internationally; no nationality restriction stated.

Award: CAD 10,000 grant per selected project, plus roughly two weeks (about 10 days) of studio workspace at the 7 Fingers Creation Centre and personalised coaching from the SAT and LAB7 teams. No application fee.

Duration: Around two weeks (10 days) of in-studio residency.

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

The Societe des arts technologiques (SAT) and LAB7 (the research-creation lab of 7 Fingers / Les 7 Doigts) offer research-creation residencies at the intersection of performing arts and technology, on the theme of human movement. Each selected project receives a CAD 10,000 grant, roughly two weeks (about 10 days) of studio workspace at the 7 Fingers Creation Centre in Montreal, and personalised coaching from the SAT and LAB7 teams. Open to non-profit organisations, collectives and independent artists working between performing arts and technological arts; the call is effectively open internationally, with no nationality restriction stated. No application fee. Results are announced in early October 2026. Application deadline: 31 August 2026, 17:00. Apply via the official open-call page.

item.title: Toronto Arts Council: Media Artists Program - Creation 2026
item.description:
Organisation: Toronto Arts Council

Location: Toronto, Canada

Award: Up to $15,000 (CAD) per artist for media-arts creation. No application fee.

Duration: Per project

Deadline: 15 Oct 2026

Project funding from the Toronto Arts Council for professional media artists to create or complete independent film, video, audio, digital, VR/AR and multimedia works, with grants up to $15,000. ELIGIBILITY: Canadian citizens, permanent residents or Protected Persons who have lived in Toronto for at least one year, are professional media artists retaining full creative control, and are not students.
